qt: to the Commission Nikos Pappas (The Left) Subject:

Recent investigations in Greece, focusing on large food and bakery chains, have been looking into alleged mechanisms of organised tax evasion, concealment of transactions through software manipulation and possible money laundering. In parallel, reports of information leaks for upcoming tax audits are being examined, raising serious issues of transparency and institutional integrity1. Article 325 TFEU states that fraud affecting the financial interests of the Union must be combatted. Directive 2006/112/EC, in particular Articles 242 and 273 thereof, provides for accounting obligations and possibilities for preventing tax evasion, while the VAT in the Digital Age (ViDA) reform package, adopted through Directive (EU) 2025/516, gradually modernises digital reporting obligations. Directive (EU) 2017/1371 establishes criminal law protection of the financial interests of the Union, under the conditions laid down therein. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

How does it assess, as part of the implementation of EU VAT legislation, the effectiveness of the existing mechanisms to prevent and detect systematic concealment of transactions and manipulation of tax data?
Does it intend, within its remit, to take further initiatives to strengthen the transparency, accountability and institutional integrity of national tax control mechanisms, ?
How does it assess the effectiveness of administrative cooperation between Member States’ tax authorities and the relevant EU mechanisms to prevent and tackle organised cross-border VAT fraud?
